sourceIssues.printed: Consider the normal surface X = Spec k[x, y, x]/(x² + xyz).
sourceIssues.correction: X = Spec k[x, y, z]/(x² + xyz), which is not normal: x² + xyz = x(x + yz), so X is the union of two smooth surfaces meeting along x = yz = 0, and its local ring at the origin is not a domain.
sourceIssues.reason: In k[x,y,z]/(x(x+yz)), the two factors give nonzero zero divisors even in the local ring at the origin; a normal local ring must be a domain. Both components are graphs isomorphic to A². Since the defining equation has initial term x², the tangent space has dimension 3 and the reduced tangent cone is the plane x=0. In the domain k[[t]], f(f+gh)=0 forces f=0 or f=-gh; with g,h in (t), f has no linear term. The y- and z-axis arcs span exactly that plane. The example works after deleting 'normal'; no claim about the cited P95 chart is needed for this check.

sourceIssues.printed: §4.2.9 defines W(α) using nonzero X_α on a Weyl-module weight space, then asserts equivalence with adjacency of weights and the symmetry (ϖ,β)∈W(α) iff (ϖ,β+α)∈W(−α); Proposition 4.2.10 uses those assertions.
sourceIssues.correction: Retain the nonzero-action definition of W(α); delete the claimed adjacent-weight equivalence and unrestricted pairwise symmetry in characteristic p. Repair Proposition 4.2.10(2) directly using the RIGHT inclusion of (4.2.7): for g=(1+εt^(⟨λ,α⟩−l)X_α)t^λ and v_β∈V(ϖ), t^⟨μ,ϖ⟩g⁻¹v_β has its X_α-term of exponent ⟨μ,ϖ⟩−⟨λ,β⟩−l. If X_αv_β≠0, integrality gives l≤⟨μ,ϖ⟩−⟨λ,β⟩, hence l≤l_α for ALL dominant weights. Under Proposition 4.2.13's minuscule-set hypothesis, the proof of k_α≥j_α uses only minuscule root strings, for which symmetry holds, and gives k_α=j_α=l_α. Thus its full equality, Remark 4.2.16 and the sign-corrected Corollary 4.2.19 survive, not just k_α=j_α. The printed proof of Proposition 4.2.10(1) outside that hypothesis still needs a valid argument; no counterexample to its numerical statement is claimed.
sourceIssues.reason: For GL₂ in characteristic p, in the divided-power basis v_i=F^(i)v_0 of Δ(p,0), wt(v_i)=(p−i,i), E v_i=(p−i+1)v_(i−1), F v_i=(i+1)v_(i+1). Thus E v_1=0 although both adjacent weights occur, while F v_0=v_1≠0, disproving also the pairwise symmetry. The proof's final range assertion fails: input v_p has E v_p=v_(p−1)≠0 but is sent to weight (−1,1−p) in Δ(0,−p)=Δ(p,0)⊗det^(−p), whose raising coefficient is p=0. However the omitted right inclusion yields the stated general bound by the inverse-matrix calculation above, without dualizing Weyl modules. For any S as in Proposition 4.2.13, this gives k_α≤l_α≤j_α; the minuscule argument gives the opposite k_α≥j_α. The earlier report overstated the reach by leaving Proposition 4.2.10(2) and the l_α equalities unestablished. V(ν)* is generally induced rather than Weyl, so Remark 4.2.8(3)'s identification with V(−w₀ν) cannot justify discarding the right inclusion.

sourceIssues.locator: Published proof of Lemma 7.2.8, p.79, definition of Bil_Hc(V) and assertion that U_σ is open; arXiv v3 p.82.
sourceIssues.printed: Bil_Hc(V) is the space of all invariant F-bilinear forms; the subset U_σ consisting of polarization forms is then asserted to be open.
sourceIssues.correction: Work in Alt_Hc(V), the F-linear subspace of invariant alternating forms. Its real extension is the product of the corresponding local alternating-form spaces. Each polarization cone U_σ is nonempty and open in that subspace, and the rational points of Alt_Hc(V), viewed as a Q-vector space, are dense in its real extension. Thus choose Ψ there with all components polarizations and take Tr_(F/Q)Ψ as in the paper. The conclusion of Lemma 7.2.8 is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: Take F=Q, G=GSp₂≅GL₂ with its usual Shimura datum, Hc=SL₂, and the fundamental Hodge embedding on V=Q²⊗Q² where G acts on the first factor and trivially on the multiplicity factor. With J the standard alternating form, invariant bilinear forms are J⊗A for arbitrary A∈M₂(Q). Such a form is alternating iff A is symmetric; with compatible sign convention the polarization cone is A symmetric positive definite. This is open in Sym₂(R), not in M₂(R): arbitrarily small nonsymmetric perturbations of I leave the cone. In general, h_σ(U(1))⊂Hc_(R,σ) makes b(x,h_σ(i)y) symmetric for invariant alternating b; positive definiteness is open there. Nonemptiness is supplied by the Cartan-involution polarization argument cited in the paper. Deligne 1979 §1.1.10 (p.253) explicitly requires symmetry after applying h(i); §1.1.18(a) (p.256) provides existence, not automatic alternation of every invariant bilinear form.

sourceIssues.correction: Replace both products by disjoint unions, identifying each factor's roots with the corresponding component of R. The Schubert varieties themselves form a product and their tangent spaces a direct sum; their root-direction index sets form disjoint unions.
sourceIssues.reason: Each Φ is a subset of R×Z, and a root belongs to exactly one simple factor. Under a product of Schubert varieties a pure root direction occurs in the tangent space of that one factor, not as a tuple choosing a direction in every factor. For G=GL₂×GL₂ and λ=μ=((1,0),(1,0)), each factor has one root direction (α,0), while the product variety P¹×P¹ has two independent root directions. The printed Cartesian product has one element, whereas the correct disjoint union has two. The factorwise reduction of the theorem is valid with this correction.
